title: Energy resolution at 250 keV from quanta statistics: does a +-23 keV (9 %) uncertainty follow from N_q fluctuations, recombination and the NR-band width?
question: For the 248 keV LZ event, what statistical energy resolution follows from NEST quanta fluctuations, photon/electron counting, recombination anticorrelation, position and lifetime corrections; how does it relate to the NR-band width, the S1-only/S2-only energies and the ER case; and how does it propagate to delta_max?
headline_result: Statistical resolution 11.4 keV (4.6 %; 10.2-12.4 over assumptions), photon-detection dominated; LZ's +-23 keV (stat) needs 4x the variance; band width worth 0.9 keV; sigma_E = 11.5 (E/248)^0.54 keV recommended
key_numbers: budget keV: photon binomial 8.5, dphe 5.4, position 4.2, SPE 2.8, quanta 1.9, S2-side <0.4; totals Nq 11.4 / S1 11.6 / 2D 11.2 / S2 56; +-23 needs S1c spread 10.9 % (model 5.4 %); band 0.0312 dex = 21.7 e = 0.93 keV; deficit 31.6 e = 1.35 (Nq) / 4.1 keV (2D, E_2D 244.4); event E_S1 248.6+-11.6, E_Nq 247.2+-11.5, E_S2 176.7+-54; ER 6.4 keV (2.6 %); sigma(delta_max,1 TeV) 2.5 vs 5.0 keV
model_or_mechanism: nestpy GetQuanta at fixed E + layered detector model (g1 binomial, dphe, SPE, extraction, SE Fano, position, e-lifetime); Nq/S1/S2 inversions and 2D Fisher estimator
confidence: high for budget and band relation; medium for absolute value (ext_eff, sigma_pos, P_dphe assumed)
